# Probe — does a local generative ladder change the finding?

*Generated by `npm run sonde` from `data/profiles.json`, measured
2026-08-20. Local generative tiers through Ollama;
`qwen3:0.6b`, `qwen3:4b`, `qwen3:8b`, scored by this
repository's own `correct()`, on the same held-out split as every other figure here.*

**Two sample sizes, and the difference is not cosmetic.** The encoder tiers carry
n=1000; the generative tiers carry n=120, because 120 cases of local
inference is roughly twenty-five minutes and no decision here needs a tighter interval
than that. Every rate below is written with its own interval and its own n, so the two
are never silently compared as if they were measured the same way.

---

## What was asked

The repository's ladder is encoder models — extractive QA and embeddings. The standing
objection, and the fair one, is that this is not LLM routing. So: put real generative
models on the same corpus, judged by the same scorer, and see whether the finding
survives.

Qwen3 at 0.6B, 4B and 8B, local through Ollama. 32B was ruled out before starting: at
4-bit it needs roughly 20 GB of weights, and this machine has 16 GB of unified memory.

## Latency, per call

| `rules` | `distilbert` | `roberta` | `qwen3:0.6b` | `qwen3:4b` | `qwen3:8b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <1 ms | 18 ms | 48 ms | 222 ms | 710 ms | 1,101 ms |

These move by 20–30 % between runs depending on what is warm, and the frozen profile
records the machine load at the moment each was taken. Treat them as an order of
magnitude, not a measurement — the same caveat the README already carries.

## The finding this changes, and why that is good news

The README's strongest sentence is that no available tier can read an address, and that
the next gain is a step and not a slope — buying exactly one field.

**A 4B model reads the address at 95.8 % [91–98], n=120.** Against `roberta`'s
32.8 % [30–36], n=1000, that is +63.0 points on
the one field the optimiser singled out, and the intervals
do not touch.

That does not refute the finding. It *pays it out.* The tool predicted, from measurement
alone, that the gain worth wanting was on the address field and that it would cost a step
change rather than more budget. Encoder to generative is exactly a step change, and it
moved exactly that field. A prediction that came true is a better result than a ceiling.

## The finding is now sharper, not weaker

At 20 cases the probe read 4B and 8B as indistinguishable on extraction. At 120 that
is wrong, and wrong in the interesting direction.

**On the address, the 8B model is worse than the 4B:**
82.5 % [75–88], n=120 against 95.8 % [91–98], n=120. The intervals
do not overlap.
Doubling the model loses 13.3 points
and costs 55 % more latency.

**On classification the same ladder is strictly monotonic**:
61.7 %, 94.2 %, 100.0 %. Bigger is better, cleanly.

Same three models, same machine, same run. Bigger is worse on one task and better on the
other. That is the thesis of this repository stated as sharply as it can be stated, and
it is measured on real generative models rather than inferred from encoders.

## The encoders were not superseded

The result that would have been easy to assume — that a generative ladder simply wins —
is false here, on 3 of 5 fields:

- **`name`: `roberta` is not beaten**, 96.6 % [95–98], n=1000 against
  91.7 % [85–95], n=120 for `qwen3:8b` — the intervals overlap, so this sample does not separate them.
- **`birth`: `rules` ties**, 100.0 % [100–100], n=1000 against
  100.0 % [97–100], n=120 for `qwen3:8b` — the intervals overlap, so this sample does not separate them.
- **`country`: `rules` ties**, 100.0 % [100–100], n=1000 against
  100.0 % [97–100], n=120 for `qwen3:4b` — the intervals overlap, so this sample does not separate them.

On accuracy alone, the best per-field assignment now spans all
3 families at once — extractive encoders, free rules, local generative —
`roberta` for the name, `rules` for the birth, `qwen3:8b` for the document, `rules` for the country, `qwen3:4b` for the address, giving
95.2 % against 83.9 % for the best
encoder-only assignment, with 2 of 5 fields still free. Which is
the argument for measuring per field, made without a sentence of advocacy.

**This average is a mean of five per-field rates measured on separate samples, not a
proportion of anything.** It carries no interval for that reason, and the per-field rates
above are the figures to quote.

## What the probe cost me in wrong answers first

Two full runs scored zero on every field before anything worked, and both were the
harness, not the model.

**Free-text generation does not work at all here.** qwen3 reasons in ordinary prose — "We
are given a document string and we need to extract…" — not inside `<think>` tags, so
`think: false` suppresses nothing and `/no_think` returns an empty string. A JSON schema
on the response is not a refinement; it is the only thing that produces a value.

**And a schema alone is not enough.** With one, the model filled the field with the
*question* ("the identity document number") or with the entire document. One worked
example in the prompt fixed both, and took the address from nothing to the rate above.

Both were my errors, recorded because this is the third time in this repository that a
broken harness has been mistaken for a broken model, and the first two cost more.

## What is not honest to claim yet

- **The probe's own first reading was wrong**, and it took the full sample to see it.
  Twenty cases said "indistinguishable on extraction"; 120 said otherwise. A
  conclusion drawn from twenty cases was confidently wrong in this repository, which is
  why every figure here carries its interval.
- **This document was itself typed by hand until 2026-08-20**,
  and eleven of its figures had gone stale against the frozen profile — including two
  sentences of conclusion. It is generated now, which is the only reason the numbers
  above can be trusted to still be the measured ones.
- **The generative tier got prompt engineering the encoders cannot receive.** A one-shot
  example and a constrained schema are not available to an extractive QA head. That is a
  property of the tier type rather than a thumb on the scale, but the comparison is not
  like-for-like and should say so.
- **The cost model does not fit a local tier.** Prices here are per thousand API calls. A
  model on your own silicon costs time and electricity, and at these latencies that is
  not a rounding error. A budget in seconds belongs beside the budget in dollars.

## What a full build would take

Ollama and the three models are installed and the harness is repository code. What
remains is the cost basis for a local tier, then figures, README, tests and demo data
regenerated. The recommendation stands: keep the encoder ladder as the default that
reproduces with no download, and the generative ladder behind `--llm`.

*Regenerate with `npm run sonde` after any re-measurement. `npm test` refuses a stale
copy.*
